question: India won its last ODI Cricket world cup in which year as of 2022?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2011.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Cricket World Cup 2011:**

__
 
• It was the **10th edition** of the Cricket World Cup (CWC).
 
• Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and India shared the hosting duties.
 
• **India and Sri Lanka **faced off in the **championship game **at Mumbai, India's Wankhede Stadium.
 
• **India won the World Cup **after an incredible campaign.
 
• **Tillakaratne Dilshan** was the **highest run scorer** in this edition of the CWC.
 
• **Zaheer Khan** and **Shahid Afridi** are jointly the **highest wicket-takers** in this edition of the CWC.
 
• The player of the tournament award went to Yuvraj Singh.
 
• After winning their first World Cup in 1983, India won their second one 28 years later.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Cricket World Cup 2023:**

 
• It is the **13th and latest edition **of the Cricket World Cup (CWC).
 
• It was the **first World Cup **of men's cricket that **India has hosted entirely**.
 
• India and Australia faced off in the championship match at Narendra Modi Stadium.
 
• **In 2023, Australia won **the Cricket World Cup for the **sixth time**.
 
• **Virat Kohli** was the highest run scorer in this edition of the CWC.
 
• **Mohammed Shami** was the highest wicket-taker in this edition of the CWC.
 
• The **player of the tournament and top run scorer was Virat Kohli**.

**Cricket World Cup 2027:**

 
• It will be the **14th edition **of the Cricket World Cup.
 
• It is scheduled to **take place in South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia **during October and November 2027.
 
• It will be co-hosted by South Africa and Zimbabwe for the second time.
 
• **Namibia **will make its **debut as a host nation**. 

A glossary of cricket terms:

 
 

 Terms
 Explanation
 
 

 Leg-Before Wicket (LBW)
 It's a way to get the batter out. In other words, the hitter is out if the umpire determines that the ball struck any portion of the batter's body—typically the leg—prior to striking the bat or missing the bat and would have struck the stumps.
 
 

 Maiden
 An over where no runs that are attributable to the bowler are scored (byes or leg-byes may be scored in this over, though, as these don't count against the bowler).
 
 

 Wide Ball
 A delivery that pitches too far away from the batsman and so proves impossible to score off. The umpire will single this by stretching his arms out horizontally; an extra will be added to the total and the ball will be bowled again.
 
 

 Bouncer
 A short-pitched ball which passes the batsman at chest or head height
 
 

 Chinaman
 A ball bowled by a left-arm slow bowler that turns into the right-hand batsman, in effect a left-arm legspinner. Named after Puss Achong.
 
 

 Mankad
 A term popular mainly in indoor cricket - but also fairly popular in Australia for outdoor cricket. Mankad is when the bowler brings his arm around and, instead of releasing the ball, runs out the non-striker by whipping off the bails. This type of dismissal is rare - and usually a warning is given to the batsman beforehand. Named after Vinod Mankad, who twice dismissed Australian Bill Brown this way.
 
 

 Doosra
 A Hindi/Urdu word which means "second" or "other", the doosra is the offspinner's version of the googly, delivered out of the back of the hand and turning away from the right-hand batsman.
